title: (Senior) Backend Engineer C++ (All genders)
description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost effective. This provides our operators with a decisive edge in highly contested environments.
We’re focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems - not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe - today.

About the team

Minerva is STARK's command and control software — the brain that connects operators to autonomous systems across multiple domains in real time. The Minerva team is a small, senior software group based in Berlin and Munich, working directly with our systems and hardware teams to build mission-critical C2 capabilities deployed in active operational environments.We move fast, ship real software, and operate under constraints most engineers never encounter — low-bandwidth networks, air-gapped devices, high-stakes decision loops. There is no room for abstraction for its own sake. Everything we build ends up in the hands of real operators in the field.

Your mission

This is not a "standard" backend role. You won't be building CRUD apps for a web store. You will be building the high-performance, low-latency engine at the heart of Minerva Frontline, our Command & Control (C2) Software, enabling mission planning and operations of Aerial and Maritime asset swarms in real world conditions.
We are looking for C++ developers to build out our core server-side architecture enabling the increasingly complex CONOPS required by NATO’s Armed forces. You will be responsible for how we maintain a global battlefield state, how we translate high-level operator intents into machine-executable actions, and how we stream real-time telemetry to the frontline.
You will work in a high-density engineering environment alongside robotics, safety, and mission planning experts. If you care about RAII, memory safety, and squeezing every ounce of performance out of real hardware in the field to ensure mission success, this is the role.
What You'll Build

- The System Brain: You will develop the core C++ services that orchestrate UAV and USV swarms, maintaining a synchronized and robust battlefield state across distributed systems.
- Mission Control APIs: You will design and implement high-performance gRPC and REST APIs that bridge the gap between our frontend C2 interface and the autonomous vehicles in the field.
- Real-Time Data Pipelines: You will build and optimize the telemetry pipelines that handle high-frequency data from diverse sensors, ensuring low-latency synchronization and delivery.
- Scalable Architecture: You will expand our current C++ architecture to support "affordable mass"—scaling from controlling 4 to 20+ vehicles simultaneously.
- Tactical Integration: You will implement military standards and protocols (such as STANAG), ensuring our systems are interoperable and battle-ready.
- Robustness & Testing: You will build and maintain the test suites, ensuring our code performs reliably under the most contested conditions.

Responsibilities

- A C++ Native: You write clean, performant Modern C++ (17/20/23). You understand the cost of every allocation and the value of a deterministic system.
- Systems-Minded: You think in terms of data flows, state machines, and concurrency. You understand that in our domain, "late data is wrong data."
- A Problem Solver: You dive deep into the details to identify, understand, and solve difficult technical problems at the hardware-software boundary.
- High Agency: You don't wait for perfect specifications. You understand the mission, look at the code, and drive the architecture forward.
- Collaborative: You thrive in a multidisciplinary team, working closely with frontend, robotics, and integration engineers to deliver a cohesive product.

Qualifications

- Experience: 5+ years of experience in backend or systems engineering, with a primary focus on high-performance C++ applications.
- C++ Expertise: Deep proficiency in Modern C++ (17 or later).
- Networking: Strong understanding of asynchronous networking, inter-process communication (IPC), and real-time data streaming.
- Industry Context: Relevant experience in Aerospace, Robotics, Automotive, Sensors, or High-Frequency Trading—any domain where software interacts with the physical world in real-time.
- Bonus Skills: Familiarity with autopilot/flight control systems (MAVLink/PX4/ArduPilot), geospatial data handling (GIS), or building safety-critical software systems.

Why Join STARK?

- Impact: Build the software that NATO militaries rely on when stakes are highest. Your code will directly influence the outcome of critical missions.
- Engineering Excellence: Work in a culture where technical rigor and architectural beauty are valued. We don't cut corners on safety or performance.
- Novelty: Solve "Genesis-stage" engineering problems for autonomous swarming that have no off-the-shelf solution.
- Growth: As we scale our platforms from the North Sea to the edges of Europe, your role and impact on the organization will grow with us.

If interested in this opportunity, send us your CV in English, and we will reach out to you soon!

title: Head of Flight Control System (FCS) (all genders)
description:
About Us

This gives our operators a decisive edge in highly contested environments. Your mission

As Head of FCS, you own STARK's flight control system: the software and firmware that fly our aircraft, and the avionics hardware it runs on. Your team develops the FCS as a core product and delivers it into multiple Loitering Munition platform developments across STARK. You build that team, across HW/SW: flight software and firmware, and avionics hardware, with product management, systems engineering and integration binding them together.

The current software is based on available libraries (e.g. PX4 or similar) and your team integrates and extends it for current and new products. The ambition is to develop own flight control laws and embedded software in future. You will work with flight dynamics and control laws from our flight sciences team, requirements and interface definitions from systems engineering, and you deliver qualified flight control systems and software releases into the platform teams for integration and flight test of prototypes, and then full production. Several aircraft programmes run in parallel and every one of them wants flight control now, so the challenge in this job is to develop a core capability and support its deployment against programme deadlines. The scope grows with the team: it starts with the flight software and widens into an own development avionics hardware. Several of the strategic decisions that shape the scope and team are open, and your mission will include making them.

Responsibilities

Team & capability build

- Develop and manage sub-teams across software and hardware, with team leads who can run their areas.

- Hire and lead both hardware and software engineering areas, building upon the current software team.

- Balance core development and platform reusability with project-specific customer deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Plan sprints and allocate capacity across parallel aircraft programmes, and keep focus on priorities with urgent deadlines and critical projects.

- Build a design verification culture of that catches problems on the bench: design reviews, code reviews, continuous integration.

- Serve as the primary point of contact for Vehicle Systems Leads, Payload Teams, and Ground Control Software teams across active projects.

Flight Control System design, integration & verification

- Architect a unified, modular FCS platform (hardware + software) capable of supporting multi-rotor, fixed-wing, and VTOL aircraft with minimal platform-specific code duplication

- Lead the development of automated Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test environments to accelerate regression testing.

- Own the safety-critical flight termination system, hardware and software, for test and development.

- Direct hardware/software co-design trade studies evaluating sensor selection (IMUs, barometers, magnetometers), processing units, bus architectures (CAN/DroneCAN, Ethernet, UART), and power redundancy schemes.

- Agree the design assurance approach with system safety and certification, oversee the production of technical documentation and means of compliance for the FCS.

- Perform FMECA (Failure Mode, Effects, and Criticality Analysis) to ensure system reliability and redundancy.

- Work with system level ground and flight testing to develop, test and analyse telemetry data for control loop tuning and design verification.

Flight software & firmware

- Lead the avionics software team, which shall own the PX4-based software integration and extension: custom modules, drivers, flight modes, failsafe logic, sensor and component interfaces.

- Deliver flight control software to new prototypes, in-production, and in-service units, managing version-control and release management to the different platforms and fleet.

- Integrate the control laws into the flight control software for each platform

- Define software development standards and processes suitable and scalable from rapid prototyping through to mass production.

Avionics hardware

- Lead the avionics hardware team, which shall take our flight-controller hardware from requirements through schematic, PCB layout, component selection and integration of sensor interfaces.

- Direct trade studies on sensor selection, processing, bus architecture (CAN/DroneCAN, Ethernet, UART, SPI), power distribution and redundancy.

- Drive EMI/EMC, signal integrity, mechanical and thermal design, environmental qualification, and design for manufacture with Production.

- Deliver flight control hardware into the HIL benches, and qualified boards and BSP into the programmes.

Qualifications

Required

- Degree in aerospace, electrical, or computer engineering, robotics, or a related field.

- 7+ years in UAV, avionics, or robotics engineering, with 2+ years of technical leadership or engineering management experience.

- Control Theory: Strong proficiency in linear/non-linear control theory (PID, LQR, MPC), flight dynamics, state estimation (Kalman Filters / EKF), and vehicle system identification.

- FCS Software: experience with PX4, Ardupilot or similar, proprietary RTOS FCS development, or real-time embedded environments.

- Avionics Hardware: Hands-on familiarity with PCB design principles, sensor integration, EMI/EMC mitigation, and communication buses (CAN, SPI, UART, Ethernet, Arinc, Milbus).

- Experience in building and managing engineering teams

- Business-fluent English; German at working level is useful, not required.

- NATO member-state citizen, eligible for German security clearance (Ü2/Ü3).

Preferred

- Experience with unmanned system development (multi-rotors, fixed-wing, VTOL-hybrid)

- Experience in developing avionics to aerospace standards (DO-178C, DO-254, ARP4754A) or equivalent Automotive or Industrial standards (IEC, etc)

- Experience with automated HIL/SIL test bench setup and test execution

- Experience running hardware-software co-development using Agile frameworks.

- Development of new flight controllers

- Leadership in a multi-programme organisation

Mindset

- Build for reuse: You solve the problem once, in a way the next three programmes can use, and you can say no to the one-off that would cost you the platform.

- Comfortable without the answer: Parts of the roadmap are still open. You make sound calls anyway and revisit them when the decisions land.

- Close to the aircraft: You go to the field, watch your builds fly, and assess the data

- Straight about risk: You say when something is not ready to fly, in front of people who want it to be.

title: Technical Product Manager (All gender)
description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionising the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop, and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective — providing operators with a decisive edge in contested environments.

We are focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems — not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe, today.

About the team

At the heart of our robotic platforms are robust sensor networks and reliable operating systems. As a Robotics Product Owner, you will be the vital link between high-level system requirements and daily engineering execution.

Your mission

You will guide a cross-functional team of hardware and software engineers through a rapidly growing portfolio of projects. By taking inputs from system engineers and program managers, you will ensure the team always has clear, actionable, and prioritized work, while keeping the broader organization informed of our technical capabilities.

Responsibilities

- Translate Needs: Work closely with system engineers and program managers to break down complex system requirements into clear, actionable user stories and acceptance criteria for the engineering team.

- Push the Backlog: Regularly align with the team lead to manage and prioritize the team's backlog across the hardware and software stack, balancing long-term foundational architecture with immediate project milestones.

- Drive Execution: Facilitate daily alignment across the team—from hardware engineers working on optics and supplier specs, to software engineers building out embedded systems and sensor overlays—to unblock work and keep sprints moving smoothly.

- Document Capabilities: Maintain clear, accessible, and up-to-date documentation of our technical capabilities, system resources, and sprint outcomes so stakeholders always know what the team can deliver.

- Evaluate & Accept Work: Review completed engineering work against requirements, navigating collaborative trade-offs when friction arises between hardware constraints, embedded software performance, and project timelines.

Qualifications

- Experience: 3+ years of experience as a Technical Product Manager, or similar roles, specifically working on hardware-software integrated products, robotics, IoT, or complex technical platforms.

- Technical Literacy: You are comfortable reviewing technical structures, navigating code repositories on GitLab, and collaborating effectively with software engineers.

- Systems Thinking: A solid understanding of the robotics and embedded tech stack. You should feel comfortable discussing sensor calibration, edge computing (like Jetson platforms), driver integration, and overall system architecture.

- Communication: Exceptional ability to communicate complex concepts clearly, acting as the bridge between deeply technical engineers and higher-level program managers.

Nice to have

- Familiarity with sensor hardware lifecycles and optics.

- Experience with embedded Linux, Jetson carrier boards, or base image configuration.

- Experience with Agile frameworks in a hardware context.

- Previous experience working in the defense, aerospace, or autonomous vehicle sectors.

We know that great candidates come from diverse backgrounds. If you don't have these exact qualifications but feel you could succeed in this role, please apply anyway.

description:

You will not merely test isolated components; rather, you will be responsible for the holistic system qualification according to military standards. In our agile start-up environment, you won't just plan test campaigns from your desk—you will actively execute them in our lab or alongside external partners.

Responsibilities

- Holistic Test Management: Independent definition, planning, preparation, and execution of environmental test campaigns

- Ideally fully Interdisciplinary Testing: Monitoring and evaluating system behavior under extreme conditions, taking mechanical, electrical, electromagnetic (EMC), and high-voltage (HV) aspects into account.

- Campaign Management: Selection, coordination, and technical supervision of external test labs and service providers, as well as the establishment and operation of in-house testing capabilities.

- Data Acquisition & Analysis: Utilization of data acquisition systems (DAQ) and specialized testing software for precise documentation and fault analysis.

- Troubleshooting & Design Feedback: Close collaboration with the R&D team (Electronics/Mechanics) to conduct immediate Root Cause Analyses (RCA) in the event of hardware or PCB failures during environmental tests, driving necessary design iterations.

Qualifications

- Educational Background: A completed degree in Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a comparable field.

- Norms & Standards: Deep knowledge of qualification according to military standards and ideally AECTP 200/400/600 (or MIL-STD-810 / MIL-STD-461). Or holistic automtive Testing

- Holistic Technical Understanding: You think across disciplines. In addition to environmental and mechanical testing (vibration/shock), you bring solid knowledge in the following areas:

- Electrical Engineering & PCB: Understanding of circuit designs and PCBs at the system level (even though the focus is on system testing, not pure PCB component testing).

- High Voltage (HV): Safe handling and practical experience with high-voltage systems.

- Electromagnetics (EMC/EMI): A foundational understanding of electromagnetic compatibility in military systems.

- Mechanical understanding of vibration, shock, thermal cycling, and humidity

Nice to have

- Defense Experience: Proven experience in the military environment or defense industry. You understand the specific requirements, processes, and mindset of this sector.

title: Test Design Engineer (All Genders)
description:
About Us

STARK is a defence technology company redefining how autonomous and electronic warfare systems are engineered and deployed. We design, build, and operationalise high-performance EW and unmanned systems that provide NATO forces with decisive advantages in contested electromagnetic environments. Our work is grounded in precision, responsibility, and uncompromising engineering discipline.

Your mission

As a Test Design Engineer (Field Engineer) within the Electronic Warfare (EW) division, you will bridge the gap between development and real-world execution. This role is heavily focused on the test design, validation, and field deployment of advanced RF communications and electronic attack (jamming) systems. You will design rigorous test methodologies, simulate contested electromagnetic environments, and lead field-testing campaigns to ensure our technologies dominate the modern battlespace.

Responsibilities

- Develop comprehensive test plans, procedures, and automated test scripts for EW systems, specifically focusing on RF communications, signals intelligence (SIGINT), and electronic countermeasures (ECM/Jamming).

- Lead and execute field-testing campaigns in complex, dynamic, and austere environments. Troubleshoot hardware, software, and RF link issues on-site.

- Design and replicate real-world threat environments using RF signal generators, channel simulators, and software-defined radios (SDRs) to test jamming efficacy and communications resilience (e.g., frequency hopping, LPI/LPD waveforms).

- Collect, process, and analyze massive datasets from field tests using MATLAB, Python, or specialized RF analysis tools to quantify system performance and identify anomalies.

- Partner with systems, hardware, and software engineering teams to feed field data back into the development loop, driving iterative design improvements.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications, Aerospace Engineering, or a highly related technical discipline.

- 3+ years of experience in RF engineering, flight test engineering, or electronic warfare testing.

- Strong foundational knowledge of RF propagation, link budgets, antenna characteristics, and modulation techniques (e.g., QAM, OFDM, FSK).

- Deep familiarity with laboratory and field test equipment, including Spectrum Analyzers, Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs), Signal Generators, and Oscilloscopes.

- Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or LabVIEW for test automation and post-test data analysis.

Nice to have

- Prior experience with specific electronic attack methodologies (e.g., barrage, spot, sweep, and DRFM-based jamming).

- Hands-on experience with Software Defined Radios (Ettus USRP, BladeRF) and tactile military communications networks.

- Familiarity with government test ranges (e.g., White Sands, China Lake) and range safety/operations protocols.

title: UAV Operations Engineer / Pilot – Data Operations (all genders)
description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective. This provides our operators with a decisive edge in highly contested environments.

We're focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems — not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe — today.

About the team

The Data Operations team owns the entire data lifecycle behind STARK's AI stack: collection, acquisition, generation, curation, and management. We run our own data-collection campaigns across Europe, evaluate new sensors and platforms, and build the internal data platform that turns raw recordings into ready-to-use datasets. Everything we produce feeds directly into the perception and autonomy systems deployed on STARK's platforms — a real data advantage is built, not bought. The team is scaling up right now: real scope, direct impact, no legacy.

Your mission

You own our data-collection flights. When the perception team needs a specific dataset — a new camera at a new angle, a lidar over specific terrain, a thermal sensor at dusk — you plan the campaign, configure and tune the platform, fly the mission, and bring clean data home. Our hardware engineer builds the rigs and mounts, our robotics engineer makes the sensors record — you make it all fly, reliably, again and again. This is a role for someone with real stick time and real PX4/ArduPilot depth: not a desk job with occasional field trips, but the other way around.

Responsibilities

- Plan and execute field data-collection campaigns across Europe: flight planning, site assessment, pre-flight checks, piloting, logging, and post-flight data offload

- Configure, tune, and troubleshoot PX4/ArduPilot flight stacks for stable, repeatable data-collection flights

- Analyze flight logs to diagnose issues and continuously improve platform reliability

- Operate sensor payloads (cameras, gimbals, lidar, GNSS/IMU) during missions and verify recordings on-site

- Keep the fleet mission-ready: maintenance, repairs, spare parts, battery management, and configuration control

- Work with our hardware and robotics engineers on payload integration — you define what the platform needs to fly well

- Maintain flight logs and campaign documentation so every flight produces usable, traceable data

- Ensure operations comply with aviation regulations (EU drone rules) and internal safety procedures

Qualifications

- Confident, experienced drone pilot with substantial real-world flight hours (multirotor; fixed-wing a plus), holding an EU A2/A3 certificate or willing to obtain quickly

- Solid practical knowledge of PX4 and/or ArduPilot: configuration, parameter tuning, log analysis, MAVLink basics

- Hands-on experience assembling, repairing, and maintaining drones — comfortable with soldering, wiring, and multimeter debugging

- Experience operating sensor payloads and ground control stations in the field

- Practical, structured, and safety-conscious — you find the loose cable before it becomes a crash

- Willingness to travel regularly for field campaigns and work outdoors in various conditions

- Good communication skills in English (German is a plus)

Nice to have

- Scripting skills (Python, Bash) for flight log processing and data offload automation

- CAD basics (Fusion 360, SolidWorks) and 3D-printing experience

- Experience with ROS/ROS2 recording setups or companion computers (Jetson, Raspberry Pi)

- Background in FPV, drone racing, RC modeling, competition teams, or maker culture

- Experience with camera settings and image quality trade-offs for data collection

- German driving license class B (field campaigns)

A note on our process: a portfolio says more than a CV here. Show us your builds and your flights — photos, flight logs, competition entries. If you don't hit every bullet point but you have been flying and fixing drones for years, we still want to hear from you.
If you're interested in building the future of European Defence with us, please send us your CV and portfolio in English. We're looking forward to meeting you!
